text:
B: Hi! Hello, can you hear me?
A: Yes, I can hear you. I'm Abena.
B: Chiara, nice to meet you! I loved your photo, by the way, you looked so calm. Like someone who has everything organised.
A: Thank you. Somebody has to be.
B: [laughs] Exactly. Where are you calling from?
A: Thornton Heath. Croydon.
B: Oh, south London. I'm in Fulham. So, the other side of the river, sort of.
A: Yes. Very much the other side.
B: Erm, so what do you do?
A: I'm a practice administrator at a GP surgery. Part-time. Rota, referrals, the systems. And you?
B: So I was brand partnerships manager at a luxury accessories label, and now I'm consulting, sort of, freelance strategy, for a candle brand. Taking a little break, to be honest, to think about what's next. Does that make sense?
A: Not entirely. What does strategy for a candle brand mean, in practice?
B: Erm. In practice... cioè, I help them with who they collaborate with. Which hotels, which influencers, how the brand looks on Instagram. It's a friend's brand, so it's quite... small. For now.
A: Is it paid?
B: Sort of. A little. Not really, honestly.
A: That's alright. I only wanted to understand.
B: No, no, it's fair. Everybody asks, and I always make it sound bigger. Sorry.
A: You don't need to apologise to me.
B: [laughs] Okay. Erm, are you from London originally?
A: Kumasi, in Ghana. I came at twenty-two. Twenty-five years now.
B: Oh, wow. I'm from Turin, eight years here. Do you go back much?
A: Every two years, usually Christmas. My mother is still there. She is getting older, and she lives alone, so... it's on my mind, you know.
B: Yes. I really understand that. My father, his health is not great, and I'm two hours away on a plane and I still feel it's too far. My mum comes to visit with a suitcase full of food, literally full, cheese, salami, everything.
A: Mine would do the same. Except it's me taking the suitcase. To the exact weight limit.
B: [laughs] To the gram!
A: To the gram. I weigh it twice.
B: I love that. Do you travel otherwise?
A: My husband and I went to Lisbon for our twentieth anniversary. It was nice. Overpriced.
B: Oh, I loved Lisbon! We stayed in this little boutique hotel in Alfama, with the terrace, the view... but yes, okay, it was expensive. The breakfast alone.
A: I had a spreadsheet. We went over on the second day.
B: [laughs] Only the second day? That's good! I would be over in the first hour.
A: I believe you.
B: Erm, do you do anything at the weekend? Like for you?
A: Choir. I sing alto at church, Methodist. Rehearsal on Thursday ran over again because half the sopranos hadn't learned the music.
B: Oh no. I go sometimes to the Italian church in Clerkenwell, when I'm homesick. I don't sing, though. Nobody would want that.
A: Everyone can learn their part. They just have to—
